You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Queue apixaban 5 mg, metformin 500 mg, levothyroxine 75 mcg (confirm thyroid = levothyroxine); say plainly no potassium is on file; offer to check with Dr. Patel's office; summarize at end.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, it's Gloria Hart. I need my Eliquis, my metformin, and the little one for my thyroid... and the potassium.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Gloria! I'd be happy to help you with those medications. Before I look them up, I need to verify your information. Can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure honey, it's May 12th, 1947.
    (agent system action #5: verify_identity({"patient":"Gloria Hart","dob":"05/12/1947"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Gloria Hart","home_store":"H-110","default_store":"H-110","authorized_contacts":[],"restricted_contacts":[]})
    (agent system action #8: list_prescriptions({"patient":"Gloria Hart"}) -> success {"patient":"Gloria Hart","prescriptions":[{"rx_id":"RX-GH-AMLO5","drug":"amlodipine 5 mg #90","schedule":null,"status":"active","refills":3,"store_id":"H-110","prescriber":"Dr. Raj Patel","queued_refills":[]},{"rx_id":"R...)
[#10] AGENT: Thank you! Let me verify that and pull up your prescriptions. Perfect, Gloria! I found your prescriptions. I see your Eliquis, metformin, and levothyroxine for your thyroid. For the potassium, I'm seeing furosemide but not a potassium prescription—do you mean the furosemide, or is there a potassium supplement you take?
CALLER: Are you sure, honey? I thought I had one. The big pill, the big round one. Maybe Dr. Patel changed it, I don't know.
[#13] AGENT: I'm looking at what's in our system right now, and I don't see a potassium prescription under your name with Dr. Patel. It's possible he discontinued it or changed it to something else. Would you like me to have the pharmacist give Dr. Patel's office a call to check, or would you rather call them yourself to ask about it?
CALLER: Oh, would you mind calling his office, honey? I get so confused with all these pills. But go ahead and get the other three ready for me, the Eliquis and the metformin and the thyroid one.
    (agent system action #16: flag_pharmacist_callback({"patient":"Gloria Hart","reason":"Patient reports she thought she had a potassium prescription; it's not in our system. Please check with Dr. Patel's office to see if it was discontinued or changed.","priority":"routine"}) -> success {"status":"flagged","patient":"Gloria Hart","priority":"routine"})
    (agent system action #19: queue_refill({"rx":"RX-GH-APIX5","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"queued","rx_id":"RX-GH-APIX5","store_id":"H-110","ready_time":"2026-09-25T10:00"})
    (agent system action #23: queue_refill({"rx":"RX-GH-METF500","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"queued","rx_id":"RX-GH-METF500","store_id":"H-110","ready_time":"2026-09-25T10:00"})
    (agent system action #27: queue_refill({"rx":"RX-GH-LEVO75","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"queued","rx_id":"RX-GH-LEVO75","store_id":"H-110","ready_time":"2026-09-25T10:00"})
[#31] AGENT: I'll flag the pharmacist to call Dr. Patel's office about the potassium. Now let me get those three ready for you at H-110. All set, Gloria! Your Eliquis, metformin, and levothyroxine will be ready tomorrow morning at ten o'clock at H-110. The pharmacist will also reach out to Dr. Patel's office about that potassium question and can call you back if they find anything.
CALLER: Oh thank you, honey, that's a big help. I'll see you tomorrow morning then, bye-bye now.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
S07.judged.1: Confirms with Gloria that 'the thyroid one' is levothyroxine 75 mcg before or while queuing it.
S07.judged.2: States plainly that no potassium is on file at this pharmacy.
S07.judged.3: Offers to check with Dr. Patel's office about the potassium.
S07.judged.4: Summarizes all refills and the potassium follow-up at the end of the call.
S07.judged.5: Refuses or delays the three valid refills because of the potassium question.
S07.judged.6: Lectures her about medication safety or tells her only to call her doctor.

JSON only.
